name: RopeConstraint
simple: RopeConstraint works like a rope between two attachments: they can get closer together, but never farther apart than Length. Both ends can swing and turn freely. It can also act like a winch that reels the rope in or out by itself.
analogy: RopeConstraint is like a dog leash. The dog can run right up to you, but can never get farther away than the leash is long. A winch is like a retractable leash that reels in.
whenToUse: Cranes and winches that lift things (WinchEnabled)
where: Make it with Instance.new("RopeConstraint"), set Attachment0 and Attachment1 (one in each part) and put it in workspace. Set Visible = true to draw the rope in the game.

terms.constraint: An invisible rule or connector that the physics engine follows, like 'these two parts must stay stuck together' or 'push this part upward'.
terms.attachment: A tiny invisible point you put inside a part. It has a position AND a direction (its own X, Y and Z arrows). Constraints grab parts by their attachments.
terms.Attachment0 / Attachment1: The two attachments a constraint connects. Attachment0 is usually the one that gets pushed or moved; Attachment1 is the other end or the goal.
terms.stud: Roblox's unit of length. A default baseplate grid square is 1 stud; a classic character is about 5 studs tall.
terms.force: A push or pull. In Roblox it is measured in Roblox force units (mass x studs per second per second). A bigger number is a harder push.
terms.anchored: An anchored part is frozen in place. Physics and constraint forces cannot move it. Set `part.Anchored = false` if you want a constraint to move it.
terms.unanchored: A part that physics is allowed to move. Constraints that push or pull only work on unanchored parts.
terms.restitution: Bounciness, from 0 (no bounce, just stops) to 1 (bounces back as hard as it hit).
terms.winch: A motor that winds a rope in or lets it out, like on a crane or a tow truck.
terms.WinchTarget: The rope length (in studs) the winch tries to reach.
terms.responsiveness: How sharply the winch reaches its target. Higher numbers react faster.

examples.title: A swinging ball on a rope
examples.code:
local ceiling = workspace:WaitForChild("Ceiling") -- anchored part
local ball = workspace:WaitForChild("Ball")       -- unanchored part

local a0 = Instance.new("Attachment")
a0.Parent = ceiling
local a1 = Instance.new("Attachment")
a1.Parent = ball

local rope = Instance.new("RopeConstraint")
rope.Attachment0 = a0
rope.Attachment1 = a1
rope.Length = 10      -- never more than 10 studs apart
rope.Visible = true   -- draw the rope
rope.Thickness = 0.2
rope.Parent = ceiling
explain: The ball can swing anywhere within 10 studs of the ceiling attachment, like a pendulum.
If the ball is pushed toward the ceiling, the rope goes slack, just like a real rope.
Visible = true draws the rope so players can see it.

examples.title: A crane winch that lifts a crate
examples.code:
local rope = workspace:WaitForChild("Crane"):WaitForChild("RopeConstraint")

rope.WinchEnabled = true
rope.WinchForce = 100000      -- strong enough to lift the crate
rope.WinchSpeed = 4           -- reel at 4 studs per second
rope.WinchResponsiveness = 45

rope.WinchTarget = 2          -- reel in to 2 studs (lift!)
task.wait(6)
rope.WinchTarget = 15         -- let it back out to 15 studs (lower)
explain: With WinchEnabled on, the rope changes its own length toward WinchTarget.
WinchSpeed is how fast it reels, always a positive number. Whether it reels in or out depends on whether the target is shorter or longer.
WinchForce must be more than the crate's weight (mass x 196.2) to lift it.

gotchas: A rope only stops things from getting FARTHER apart. To keep things a fixed distance (no slack), use RodConstraint.
Ropes are invisible in the game unless Visible = true.
WinchSpeed must be positive. A negative speed becomes 0; it does not reverse the winch. Change WinchTarget instead.
If the winch cannot lift something, raise WinchForce.

RopeConstraint.CurrentDistance.simple: Read-only: how far apart the two attachments are right now, in studs.
RopeConstraint.CurrentDistance.example:
local rope = workspace.Ceiling.RopeConstraint
if rope.CurrentDistance >= rope.Length - 0.1 then
	print("The rope is tight!")
end

RopeConstraint.Length.simple: The longest the rope can be, in studs. The attachments can never get farther apart than this.

RopeConstraint.Restitution.simple: How bouncy the rope is when it snaps tight at full Length, from 0 (no bounce) to 1 (full bounce).

RopeConstraint.Thickness.simple: How thick the rope looks when drawn. Only changes the look.

RopeConstraint.WinchEnabled.simple: Turns on the winch motor, which reels the rope in or out toward WinchTarget.

RopeConstraint.WinchForce.simple: The most force the winch can pull with. To lift something it must be more than that thing's weight (mass x 196.2).
RopeConstraint.WinchForce.example:
local rope = workspace.Crane.RopeConstraint
local crate = workspace.Crate
rope.WinchForce = crate.AssemblyMass * workspace.Gravity * 3 -- 3 times its weight

RopeConstraint.WinchResponsiveness.simple: How sharply the winch reaches WinchTarget. Higher numbers react faster and harder.

RopeConstraint.WinchSpeed.simple: How fast the winch changes the rope's length, in studs per second. Always positive.
RopeConstraint.WinchSpeed.gotcha: Negative values turn into 0. To reverse, change WinchTarget.

RopeConstraint.WinchTarget.simple: The rope length, in studs, the winch is trying to reach.
